descriptionChirho: Marks the definite direct object of a verb, indicating that the following noun is the accusative complement. This is the primary and overwhelmingly dominant function of אֵת, appearing both independently and with the conjunctive waw prefix (וְאֵת). Includes all pronominal suffix forms (אֹתוֹ 'him', אֹתָהּ 'her', אֹתָם 'them', אֹתִי 'me', אֹתְךָ 'you [ms]', אֹתָנוּ 'us', etc.) which serve as accusative pronoun objects.

Preposition meaning 'with, beside, near, in the company of' — homographic with but etymologically and functionally distinct from the direct object marker. Governs a noun or pronominal suffix to express accompaniment or proximity (e.g., אִתּוֹ 'with him', אִתְּךָ 'with you'). Distinguished from the accusative particle by context, vocalization (אֶת vs. אֵת in some traditions), and semantic role.
